You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.

## The question
"What happens after the first map is made, when someone asks a follow-up question or asks about a separate part of the code? How does the map get updated?"

## What a good map is
- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.
- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.
- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").
- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).
- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).
- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").
- When the trail stops, or something that should be connected isn't, record an `absence`: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.
- Code that exists but isn't reached from the start can still be boxes. Don't draw arrows that don't exist; use an absence.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>" (methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member, e.g. "src/db.ts#db.update").
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)
- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows → the path → the problem, if there is one → what it means.
- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it's about), optional `terms` it uses that need defining, and `ask` with 1–2 good next questions.
- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you're confident in.

12	export type Answer = {

41	function selectionLines(map: CodeMap, s: Selection): SelectionLine[] {
42	  const nodes = new Map(map.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
43	  const label = (id: string) => nodes.get(id)?.name ?? id;
44	  return [
45	    ...(s.nodes ?? []).filter((id) => nodes.has(id)).map((id) => ({ id, label: `box "${label(id)}"` })),
46	    ...(s.edges ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
47	      const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
48	      return e ? [{ id, label: `arrow "${e.label}" from "${label(e.from)}" to "${label(e.to)}"` }] : [];
49	    }),
50	    ...(s.absences ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
51	      const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
52	      return a ? [{ id, label: `missing connection: ${a.claim}` }] : [];
53	    }),
54	  ];
55	}

57	/** The map without the given ids (and without arrows or tour mentions that point at removed boxes). */
58	function without(map: CodeMap, ids: ReadonlySet<string>): CodeMap {
59	  const nodes = map.nodes.filter((n) => !ids.has(n.id));
60	  const kept = new Set(nodes.map((n) => n.id));
61	  const edges = map.edges.filter((e) => !ids.has(e.id) && kept.has(e.from) && kept.has(e.to));
62	  const absences = map.absences.filter((a) => !ids.has(a.id) && (!a.between || (kept.has(a.between.from) && kept.has(a.between.to))));
63	  const areas = map.areas.filter((a) => !ids.has(a.id) || nodes.some((n) => n.area === a.id));
64	  const live = new Set([...nodes, ...edges, ...absences, ...areas].map((x) => x.id));
65	  const tour = map.tour.map((t) => ({
66	    ...t,
67	    focus: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(t.focus).map(([k, v]) => [k, (v as string[]).filter((id) => live.has(id))])),
68	  }));
69	  const parsed = parseMap({ ...map, areas, nodes, edges, absences, tour });
70	  return parsed.ok ? parsed.map : map;
71	}
72	
73	function statusOf(report: CheckReport, id: string): RefStatus['status'] {
74	  const c = report.nodes[id] ?? report.edges[id] ?? report.absences[id];
75	  return c ? c.status : 'unknown';
76	}

78	export async function answer(o: AnswerOptions): Promise<{ answer: Answer; map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport; sessionId: string | null }> {
79	  const before = check(o.map, o.root);

82	    schema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,

90	  if (!parsed.success) throw new Error(`Claude's answer couldn't be read: ${parsed.error.issues.slice(0, 3).map((i) => i.message).join('; ')}`);
91	  const raw = parsed.data;

96	  if (raw.add) {

98	    if (merged.ok) {
99	      const old = mapIds(o.map);
100	      added = [...mapIds(merged.map)].filter((id) => !old.has(id));
101	      map = merged.map;

113	    }
114	    map = without(map, new Set(failed));
115	    report = check(map, o.root);
116	    const live = mapIds(map);
117	    added = added.filter((id) => live.has(id));
118	  }
119	
120	  let fix: FixProposal | null = null;
121	  if (raw.fix) {
122	    const proposed = proposeFix(o.root, map, raw.fix);
123	    if (proposed.ok) fix = proposed.proposal;
124	    else problems.push(...proposed.problems.map((p) => `The proposed fix can't be applied: ${p}`));
125	  }
126

128	  const result: Answer = {
129	    id: `ans-${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}`,
130	    question: o.question,
131	    selection: o.selection,
132	    concept: raw.concept,
133	    how: raw.how,
134	    code: raw.code,
135	    refs: [...new Set(raw.refs)].map((id) => ({ id, status: statusOf(report, id) })),

1	// Changing a map after it's made: what the explainer finds is added, a fix's new connection is drawn, a missing
2	// connection that a fix closed is dropped. Every change goes back through `parseMap`, so ids stay unique and references
3	// stay valid.
4	import { parseMap, type CodeMap, type ParseResult } from './format';
5	
6	/** New areas, boxes, arrows and missing connections, as the model wrote them (validated on merge). */
7	export type MapAdditions = { areas?: unknown[]; nodes?: unknown[]; edges?: unknown[]; absences?: unknown[] };
8	
9	export function addToMap(map: CodeMap, add: MapAdditions): ParseResult {
10	  return parseMap({
11	    ...map,
12	    areas: [...map.areas, ...(add.areas ?? [])],
13	    nodes: [...map.nodes, ...(add.nodes ?? [])],
14	    edges: [...map.edges, ...(add.edges ?? [])],
15	    absences: [...map.absences, ...(add.absences ?? [])],
16	  });
17	}
18	
19	export function removeAbsences(map: CodeMap, ids: readonly string[]): CodeMap {
20	  const drop = new Set(ids);
21	  return {
22	    ...map,
23	    absences: map.absences.filter((a) => !drop.has(a.id)),
24	    tour: map.tour.map((t) => (t.focus.absences ? { ...t, focus: { ...t.focus, absences: t.focus.absences.filter((id) => !drop.has(id)) } } : t)),
25	  };
26	}
27	
28	/** Ids of everything in the map, for picking new ones. */
29	export function mapIds(map: CodeMap): Set<string> {
30	  return new Set([...map.areas, ...map.nodes, ...map.edges, ...map.absences, ...map.tour].map((x) => x.id));
31	}
32	
33	export function freshId(map: CodeMap, prefix: string): string {
34	  const taken = mapIds(map);
35	  for (let i = 1; ; i++) if (!taken.has(`${prefix}${i}`)) return `${prefix}${i}`;
36	}
37	
38	/** A short, file-safe id for a map from its question. */
39	export function slugify(question: string): string {
40	  const slug = question
41	    .toLowerCase()
42	    .replace(/['’]/g, '')
43	    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
44	    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
45	    .split('-')
46	    .filter((w) => !['what', 'happens', 'when', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'does', 'do', 'how', 'is', 'are', 'it', 'go', 'out'].includes(w))
47	    .slice(0, 6)
48	    .join('-');
49	  return slug || 'map';
50	}
51

59	export async function startServer(o: ServerOptions): Promise<CodemapServer> {
60	  const root = fs.realpathSync(o.root);
61	  const agent = o.agent ?? sdkAgent;
62	  const token = o.token ?? crypto.randomBytes(18).toString('base64url');
63	  const viewerDir = o.viewerDir ?? DEFAULT_VIEWER;
64	  const store = createStore(root);
65	  const jobs = new Map<string, JobState>();
66	  const failures = new Map<string, { question: string; error: string }>();
67	  const answers = new Map<string, Answer[]>();
68	  const proposals = new Map<string, { mapId: string; proposal: FixProposal }>();
69	  const applied = new Map<string, { mapId: string; applied: AppliedFix; mapBefore: CodeMap; edgeId: string | null; closed: string[] }>();
70	  /** Where each fix on a map stands (fixes not listed were rejected), so a reloaded page shows Approve or Undo. */
71	  const fixStates = (mapId: string): Record<string, { status: 'proposed' | 'applied'; edgeId?: string | null; closed?: string[] }> => ({
72	    ...Object.fromEntries([...proposals].filter(([, p]) => p.mapId === mapId).map(([id]) => [id, { status: 'proposed' as const }])),
73	    ...Object.fromEntries([...applied].filter(([, a]) => a.mapId === mapId).map(([id, a]) => [id, { status: 'applied' as const, edgeId: a.edgeId, closed: a.closed }])),

89	    return report;
90	  };
91	  const errorText = (err: unknown) => (err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));

93	  function startMap(question: string): string {
94	    const q = question.trim();
95	    if (!q) throw new HttpError(400, 'Ask a question to map.');
96	    const id = store.newId(q, new Set([...jobs.keys(), ...failures.keys()]));
97	    jobs.set(id, { kind: 'make', question: q, progress: [] });
98	    broadcast({ type: 'job', mapId: id, job: 'make', status: 'started', question: q });
99	    void (async () => {
100	      try {
101	        const r = await makeMap({ root, question: q, agent, model: o.model, onProgress: progress(id, 'make') });
102	        const now = new Date().toISOString();

105	          map: r.map,
106	        };
107	        store.save(stored);
108	        jobs.delete(id);
109	        publishMap(stored);
110	        broadcast({ type: 'job', mapId: id, job: 'make', status: 'done', question: q });
111	      } catch (err) {
112	        jobs.delete(id);
113	        failures.set(id, { question: q, error: errorText(err) });
114	        broadcast({ type: 'job', mapId: id, job: 'make', status: 'failed', question: q, error: errorText(err) });
115	      }
116	    })();
117	    return id;
118	  }

120	  function startAsk(mapId: string, question: string, selection: Selection) {
121	    const stored = store.get(mapId);
122	    if (!stored) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
123	    if (jobs.has(mapId)) throw new HttpError(409, 'Claude is still working on this map. Try again when it finishes.');
124	    const q = question.trim();
125	    if (!q) throw new HttpError(400, 'Ask a question.');
126	    jobs.set(mapId, { kind: 'ask', question: q, progress: [] });

128	    void (async () => {
129	      try {
130	        const r = await answer({ root, map: stored.map, selection, question: q, agent, session: stored.meta.explainerSession, model: o.model, onProgress: progress(mapId, 'ask') });
131	        if (r.answer.fix) proposals.set(r.answer.fix.id, { mapId, proposal: r.answer.fix });
132	        const latest = store.get(mapId) ?? stored;
133	        const next: StoredMap = {
134	          meta: { ...latest.meta, explainerSession: r.sessionId, cost: latest.meta.cost + r.answer.cost, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() },
135	          map: r.answer.added.length ? r.map : latest.map,
136	        };
137	        store.save(next);
138	        (answers.get(mapId) ?? answers.set(mapId, []).get(mapId)!).push(r.answer);
139	        jobs.delete(mapId);

141	        broadcast({ type: 'answer', mapId, answer: r.answer });
142	        broadcast({ type: 'job', mapId, job: 'ask', status: 'done', question: q });
143	      } catch (err) {
144	        jobs.delete(mapId);
145	        broadcast({ type: 'job', mapId, job: 'ask', status: 'failed', question: q, error: errorText(err) });
146	      }
147	    })();
148	  }

150	  function approveFix(mapId: string, fixId: string) {
151	    const p = proposals.get(fixId);
152	    if (!p || p.mapId !== mapId) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such fix waiting for approval.');
153	    if (jobs.has(mapId)) throw new HttpError(409, 'Claude is still working on this map. Try again when it finishes.');
154	    const stored = store.get(mapId);
155	    if (!stored) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
156	    const r = applyFix(root, p.proposal);
157	    if (!r.ok) {

159	      throw new HttpError(409, 'The fix could not be applied.', { problems: r.problems });
160	    }
161	    proposals.delete(fixId);
162	    const c = connectAfterFix(root, stored.map, p.proposal);
163	    applied.set(fixId, { mapId, applied: r.applied, mapBefore: stored.map, edgeId: c.edgeId, closed: c.closed });
164	    const next: StoredMap = { meta: { ...stored.meta, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, map: c.map };
165	    store.save(next);
166	    const report = publishMap(next);
167	    broadcast({ type: 'fix', mapId, fixId, status: 'applied', edgeId: c.edgeId, closed: c.closed });
168	    return { edgeId: c.edgeId, closed: c.closed, files: r.applied.written.map((w) => w.file), summary: report.summary };
169	  }

171	  function undo(mapId: string, fixId: string) {
172	    const a = applied.get(fixId);
173	    if (!a || a.mapId !== mapId) throw new HttpError(404, 'No applied fix to undo.');
174	    const r = undoFix(root, a.applied);

178	    const stored = store.get(mapId);
179	    if (stored) {

181	      store.save(next);
182	      publishMap(next);
183	    }
184	    broadcast({ type: 'fix', mapId, fixId, status: 'undone' });
185	  }

189	  const hosts = () => new Set([`127.0.0.1:${port}`, `localhost:${port}`]);
190	  const hostOk = (req: http.IncomingMessage) => hosts().has(req.headers.host ?? '');
191	  const originOk = (req: http.IncomingMessage) => !req.headers.origin || [...hosts()].some((h) => req.headers.origin === `http://${h}`);
192	  const tokenOk = (given: unknown) => typeof given === 'string' && given.length === token.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(given), Buffer.from(token));
193	
194	  const json = (res: http.ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown) => {
195	    res.writeHead(status, { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'cache-control': 'no-store' });
196	    res.end(JSON.stringify(body));
197	  };
198	  const readBody = (req: http.IncomingMessage) =>
199	    new Promise<Record<string, unknown>>((resolve, reject) => {
200	      let size = 0;
201	      const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
202	      req.on('data', (c: Buffer) => {
203	        size += c.length;
204	        if (size > MAX_BODY) reject(new HttpError(413, 'Request too large.'));
205	        else chunks.push(c);
206	      });
207	      req.on('end', () => {
208	        try {

210	          resolve(text ? (JSON.parse(text) as Record<string, unknown>) : {});
211	        } catch {
212	          reject(new HttpError(400, 'Request body must be JSON.'));
213	        }
214	      });
215	      req.on('error', reject);
216	    });
217	  const asSelection = (v: unknown): Selection => {
218	    const s = (v ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;

221	  };

223	  async function api(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse, url: URL) {
224	    const parts = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(1); // after "api"
225	    const m = req.method ?? 'GET';
226	    if (parts[0] !== 'maps') throw new HttpError(404, 'Not found.');
227	    const mapId = parts[1];
228	    if (!mapId) {
229	      if (m === 'GET') {
230	        const active = [...jobs].filter(([, j]) => j.kind === 'make').map(([id, j]) => ({ id, question: j.question }));
231	        return json(res, 200, { repo: path.basename(root), maps: store.list(), making: active });
232	      }
233	      if (m === 'POST') {
234	        const body = await readBody(req);
235	        return json(res, 202, { id: startMap(String(body.question ?? '')) });
236	      }
237	    }
238	    if (mapId && !/^[a-z0-9-]{1,80}$/.test(mapId)) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
239	    if (mapId && parts.length === 2 && m === 'GET') {
240	      const stored = store.get(mapId);
241	      const job = jobs.get(mapId) ?? null;
242	      if (!stored) {
243	        if (job || failures.has(mapId)) return json(res, 200, { meta: null, map: null, report: null, job, failure: failures.get(mapId) ?? null, answers: [] });
244	        throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
245	      }
246	      return json(res, 200, { ...stored, report: check(stored.map, root), job, failure: null, answers: answers.get(mapId) ?? [], fixes: fixStates(mapId) });
247	    }
248	    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'ask' && m === 'POST') {
249	      const body = await readBody(req);

251	      return json(res, 202, { ok: true });
252	    }
253	    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'recheck' && m === 'POST') {
254	      const stored = store.get(mapId);
255	      if (!stored) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
256	      return json(res, 200, { report: publishMap(stored) });
257	    }
258	    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'fixes' && parts[3] && m === 'POST') {
259	      const fixId = parts[3];
260	      if (parts[4] === 'approve') return json(res, 200, approveFix(mapId, fixId));
261	      if (parts[4] === 'undo') { undo(mapId, fixId); return json(res, 200, { ok: true }); }
262	      if (parts[4] === 'reject') {
263	        if (proposals.get(fixId)?.mapId !== mapId) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such fix waiting for approval.');
264	        proposals.delete(fixId);
265	        broadcast({ type: 'fix', mapId, fixId, status: 'rejected' });
266	        return json(res, 200, { ok: true });
267	      }
268	    }
269	    throw new HttpError(404, 'Not found.');
270	  }

272	  function serveStatic(res: http.ServerResponse, pathname: string) {
273	    const index = path.join(viewerDir, 'index.html');
274	    if (!fs.existsSync(index)) {
275	      res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' });
276	      return res.end('<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><title>codemap</title><p style="font:16px system-ui;margin:40px">The viewer isn\'t built yet. Run <code>npm run build</code> in the codemap repo, then reload.</p>');
277	    }
278	    const rel = decodeURIComponent(pathname).replace(/^\/+/, '');
279	    const file = path.resolve(viewerDir, rel);
280	    const inside = file.startsWith(path.resolve(viewerDir) + path.sep);
281	    const target = inside && rel.startsWith('assets/') && fs.existsSync(file) && fs.statSync(file).isFile() ? file : index;
282	    res.writeHead(200, {
283	      'content-type': TYPES[path.extname(target)] ?? 'application/octet-stream',
284	      'cache-control': target === index ? 'no-store' : 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable',
285	      'x-content-type-options': 'nosniff',
286	      ...(target === index ? { 'content-security-policy': "default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:* ws://localhost:*; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'" } : {}),
287	    });
288	    fs.createReadStream(target).pipe(res);
289	  }

292	    void (async () => {

1	// Maps on disk, in the target repo: `.codemap/maps/<id>.json`. Commit them to share; teammates re-check them against
2	// their own copy of the code when they open them.
3	import * as fs from 'node:fs';
4	import * as path from 'node:path';
5	import { parseMap, slugify, type CodeMap } from '@codemap/core';
6	
7	export type MapMeta = {
8	  id: string;
9	  question: string;
10	  createdAt: string;
11	  updatedAt: string;
12	  commit: string | null;
13	  makerSession: string | null;
14	  explainerSession: string | null;
15	  cost: number;
16	};
17	export type StoredMap = { meta: MapMeta; map: CodeMap };
18	
19	const ID = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,80}$/;
20	
21	export function createStore(root: string) {
22	  const base = path.join(root, '.codemap');
23	  const dir = path.join(base, 'maps');
24	
25	  const ensure = () => {
26	    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
27	    const ignore = path.join(base, '.gitignore');
28	    // Maps are worth committing; scratch output is not.
29	    if (!fs.existsSync(ignore)) fs.writeFileSync(ignore, 'fixes/\nws-modules/\n');
30	  };
31	  const file = (id: string) => {
32	    if (!ID.test(id)) throw new Error(`Not a map id: ${id}`);
33	    return path.join(dir, `${id}.json`);
34	  };
35	
36	  return {
37	    dir,
38	    get(id: string): StoredMap | null {
39	      let raw: { meta?: MapMeta; map?: unknown };
40	      try {
41	        raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file(id), 'utf8'));
42	      } catch {
43	        return null;
44	      }
45	      const parsed = parseMap(raw.map);
46	      return parsed.ok && raw.meta ? { meta: raw.meta, map: parsed.map } : null;
47	    },
48	    save(stored: StoredMap): void {
49	      ensure();
50	      const target = file(stored.meta.id);
51	      const tmp = `${target}.tmp`;
52	      fs.writeFileSync(tmp, `${JSON.stringify(stored, null, 2)}\n`);
53	      fs.renameSync(tmp, target);
54	    },
55	    list(): MapMeta[] {
56	      if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
57	      return fs
58	        .readdirSync(dir)
59	        .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
60	        .flatMap((f) => {
61	          try {
62	            const meta = (JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), 'utf8')) as { meta?: MapMeta }).meta;
63	            return meta ? [meta] : [];
64	          } catch {
65	            return [];
66	          }
67	        })
68	        .sort((a, b) => b.updatedAt.localeCompare(a.updatedAt));
69	    },
70	    /** A new id for a question, unique among saved maps and ids already handed out. */
71	    newId(question: string, taken: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set()): string {
72	      const base = slugify(question);
73	      for (let i = 1; ; i++) {
74	        const id = i === 1 ? base : `${base}-${i}`;
75	        if (!taken.has(id) && !fs.existsSync(file(id))) return id;
76	      }
77	    },
78	  };
79	}
80	
81	export type Store = ReturnType<typeof createStore>;

28	/** A plain-English progress line for a tool call, with paths relative to the repo. */

31	  if (name === 'Read') return { kind: 'read', text: `Reading ${rel(input.file_path)}` };
32	  if (name === 'Grep') return { kind: 'search', text: `Searching for "${String(input.pattern ?? '')}"${input.path ? ` in ${rel(input.path)}` : ''}` };
33	  if (name === 'Glob') return { kind: 'list', text: `Looking for files matching ${String(input.pattern ?? '')}` };
34	  return null;
35	}

37	/** Refuse secret files, and keep repo-wide searches away from them. */
38	export function secretGuard(cwd: string): HookCallback {
39	  return async (input) => {
40	    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
41	    const ti = (i.tool_input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
42	    const target = typeof ti.file_path === 'string' ? ti.file_path : typeof ti.path === 'string' ? ti.path : null;
43	    const rel = target ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, target)) : null;

48	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Secret files are never read.' } };
